title: LED luminaires: Malaysia (ST / SIRIM) vs China
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.target_requirement: Malaysia applies ST-led energy-efficiency expectations for many imported lighting products and may require Star label submission based on category.
target_standards: Energy Commission (ST) energy-efficiency programs for imported products
SIRIM support for Star labeling process
rows.china_equivalent: China uses its own category frameworks for energy efficiency and labeling, not identical to Malaysia pathways.
china_standards: China energy-efficiency rules for lighting products
rows.gap: Do not treat Chinese label files as direct Malaysia proof. Map every class to local Star logic before release.

mandatory_status.cn: regulated by national energy rules in China

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Build a class-by-class energy dossier and verify Star applicability before customs filing.

rows.target_requirement: Malaysia expects importer-facing responsibility documentation and local contact alignment for compliance acceptance.
target_standards: Importer submission records in local format
rows.china_equivalent: Chinese export declarations are usually producer oriented and differ from Malaysia importer-registration practice.
china_standards: Product declaration practice in Chinese export channels
rows.gap: Prepare Malaysia-style importer packets even when Chinese technical declarations are complete.
rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Keep importer declarations, sign-off notes, and contact routing aligned to Malaysia process timelines.

rows.target_requirement: Malaysia aligns imported LED product EMC checks with ST and SIRIM recognition pathways, usually requiring traceable test evidence.
rows.china_equivalent: China applies GB/T emission/immunity routes for luminaires and related electrical equipment, which must be converted for Malaysian import review.
rows.gap: Expect local mapping work because report templates and acceptance language often differ by authority.

mandatory_status.target: required for classes under EMC control

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Prepare a clause-by-clause EM interference and immunity mapping between GB/T and Malaysia-facing routes.

rows.target_requirement: Where lighting products include wireless or remote features, Malaysia may require MCMC-related review separate from core electrical approvals.
target_standards: MCMC telecom and radio operation rules
Wireless product handling in product import
rows.china_equivalent: China also applies its own telecom-radio filing process for such functions, which does not automatically satisfy Malaysian MCMC needs.
china_standards: China telecom and radio management process
Wireless module local filing in China
rows.gap: Prepare dual-track compliance if the model contains any wireless capability.
rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Separate telecom review packets early for remote-control and wireless-enabled luminaire SKUs.

rows.target_requirement: Malaysia-facing evaluations commonly require photobiological classification evidence for LED luminaires in long-term human exposure contexts.
rows.china_equivalent: China also references IEC 62471 photobiological methods, but Malaysia reviewers may request local phrasing and labeling treatment.
china_standards: China photobiological test practice for lighting
rows.gap: Expect extra annotation of user exposure and environment details for Malaysia submissions.

mandatory_status.cn: commonly required where photobiological testing is used

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Align classification statement wording with Malaysia assessor expectations before release.

rows.target_requirement: Market-facing literature in Malaysia often adds flicker and blue-light risk notes for prolonged-use applications.
target_standards: Local market literature guidance for photobiological effects
rows.china_equivalent: Chinese market declarations can include such risks, but wording and submission format often differ for Malaysia.
rows.gap: Translate risk sections and align metric references to the local reviewer style before customs handoff.
rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Add clear user-scenario risk labels when products are intended for long dwell-time areas.

rows.target_requirement: Malaysia often accepts product-level declaration workflows, while strict RoHS-style legal text is not always unified for all categories.
target_standards: Supplier declaration and buyer requirement packets
rows.china_equivalent: China enforces RoHS-type restrictions in covered categories and expects concentration declarations by supplier.
rows.gap: Build Malaysia-facing restricted-substances claims that can coexist with China CoCs for the same product.
rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Keep one controlled-substance matrix per model and keep declaration date/version aligned.

rows.target_requirement: Some Malaysian commercial buyers and public projects still ask for explicit mercury and heavy-metal exclusions in LED product dossiers.
rows.china_equivalent: China channels may rely on RoHS and related RoHS-like frameworks for heavy metals, which can be mirrored with stricter Malaysian buyer filters.
rows.gap: Use buyer-level matrices when Malaysian tender or project rules add tighter thresholds than statutory text.
rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Add an annex specifying threshold handling for mercury and heavy-metal values in each product family.

rows.target_requirement: Malaysia-facing submissions often check that one declaration set is consistent across test report, invoice, and import packet.
rows.china_equivalent: China declarations can be internally consistent, yet Malaysia checks still require synchronized versioning for all submitted artifacts.
china_standards: Supplier declaration governance in China export
rows.gap: Align release version, declaration date, and file naming before filing to avoid Malaysia pre-clearance delays.
rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Use one harmonized declaration package for both Chinese and Malaysian channels when data are unchanged.

rows.requirement: ST CoA and SIRIM safety certification
rows.target_requirement: Malaysia market entry for LED luminaires commonly requires ST CoA and may require SIRIM-linked safety recognition depending on category.
target_standards: ST and SIRIM safety documentation process
rows.china_equivalent: China uses GB 7000 and related IEC-adopted standards for safety class evidence, usually not a direct replacement for ST pathways.
rows.gap: Use Chinese test reports as technical support but do not claim ST equivalence without explicit Malaysia mapping.
rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Keep one ST CoA packet per model family with traceable test dates and valid signatures.

rows.requirement: MS IEC safety references and voltage framing
rows.target_requirement: Malaysia references MS IEC 60598, MS IEC 62471, and related standards, while also checking operation at 240 V and local mains framing.
rows.china_equivalent: China references equivalent IEC and GB safety standards, but the nominal voltage context differs from Malaysia’s 240 V market frame.
rows.gap: Prepare explicit voltage adaptation and insulation evidence when a model designed for 220/380 V is redirected to 240 V use.
rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Verify voltage assumptions and protective class declarations against the Malaysia-use manual before final dispatch.
